findings.description: v1.2 ships no in-product administrative recovery for an item whose active image content hash changes: a host refresh (full POST /Library/Refresh or a targeted per-item FullRefresh) that re-adopts the local sidecar poster desynchronises the served image from the plugin's recorded active identity, and the fail-closed ownership gate then suppresses further automatic publication for that item. The behaviour is a carry-forward of F-21.4-2/F-21.9-2, independently re-observed by task 21.13 (F-21.13-2, LOW, open), and is documented in the pinned-host procedure and the release record, but it is NOT registered in docs/limitations/00-index.md (no ownership/recovery item exists there; P5 covers only orphaned pre-release state and the uninstall drain). The owner-facing recovery path or an explicit out-of-band decision remains open and PLANS.md assigns no task to it.
evidence: docs/implementation/21.13/live-verification.json finding F-21.13-2 (LOW, open) and its corrected detail: the served Primary reverted from the published badge to the source sidecar while the artwork-state record still asserted Published; no OwnershipLost transition claimed
docs/implementation/21.13/reviewer-report.attempt-2.json (substance accepted as a legitimate release limitation; owner-facing recovery or out-of-band decision left to the release review/owner)
docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md lines 342-352 ('The v1.2 product has no in-product recovery trigger for an item already in OwnershipLost') and lines 457-475 (targeted-refresh caution)
docs/changelog/v1.2.0.md release section: F-21.13-2 recorded as a carried operational bound
docs/limitations/00-index.md and accepted.md: no ownership-recovery item registered
findings.recommended_action: Register this limitation in docs/limitations/accepted.md with an index row in docs/limitations/00-index.md (a new ID, e.g. V12-F7-2, or an extension of P5) naming the consequence and this evidence, or record an explicit user decision that recovery is out of band; fold it into the release commit. Documentation only: it does not affect the verified artifact, code, or the ship decision.

observations.observation: Artifact re-derivation repeatedly left superseded identities or review pointers live in current documentation, generating a recurring finding class across the release: 21.8-REV-1/21.8-TQ-1, 21.12-REV-10/21.12-TQ-1, 21.6-REV-6, PR15-03/PR15-04 (attempt-1 evidence pointers), and R-21.9-1 (stale cache attribution). Each re-derivation required a follow-up sweep of docs/testing, docs/release, the changelog, and ADR notes.
observations.proposed_change: Add a required step to the corrective/re-derivation task template in docs/agent-contracts.md (and the orchestrator's corrective-task brief): after any artifact re-derivation, sweep docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md, docs/release/build-and-release.md, docs/changelog/v1.2.0.md and the ADR implementation notes for the superseded hash and mark each occurrence superseded. Optionally extend scripts/check-docs.sh to flag a superseded archive hash presented without a superseded marker.
observations.rationale: Five-plus occurrences in one release; the sweeps cost review rounds (including one HIGH finding's rework) that a single mechanical check would prevent.

observations.observation: Phase-level orchestration aggregates were repeatedly incomplete or inconsistent until a reviewer forced a gate-commit correction: P16-F2 (record-keeping), P17-F1 (aggregate sum off by 5.2e-8), PR-19-02 (aggregate missing, phase-reviewer invocation not recorded), and PR-20-02/PR-20-03/PR-20-04 (aggregate stale, rework invisible, prose contradicting its own rework array). The Phase 20 case required a dedicated gate-commit reconciliation.
evidence: docs/implementation/phase-20/orchestration.json (reconciled: 13 invocations, 1 rework round, phase_review points at attempt 2)
observations.proposed_change: Extend scripts/check-agents.sh to validate, for phases 20 and later, that the phase aggregate's invocation count, rework rounds, first-pass rate and recorded cost equal the sums of the task-level orchestration records and that the phase-reviewer invocation is present; fail the doc gate otherwise.
observations.rationale: The contract already requires consistency (docs/agent-contracts.md 'Phase-level orchestration record'), but nothing enforces it; the checks are mechanical and the current manual pass produced four separate defects.

observations.observation: Security findings that a phase-level security review left open as LOW/MEDIUM were not dispositioned (fix vs accept) until the release security review, where the user then chose to fix them; the late fix invalidated the artifact, live matrix, and security review and forced full re-derivations (21.7 -> 21.8-21.10, then 21.11 -> 21.12-21.14). SEC-21.5-01 (redirect) had existed since V1 and was found only at 21.5; the 15.4 review had already recorded the log-subject residuals (SR-15.4-01/02, phase-15 PR15-01) that resurfaced as SEC-21.5-02/03.
observations.proposed_change: In docs/agent-contracts.md, require the orchestrator at each phase gate to record an explicit disposition (fix-now / accept-with-register-entry / defer-with-rationale, with the user as owner for accept) for every new security finding raised by that phase's task or phase security reviews, before the next phase starts.
observations.rationale: The release phase absorbed two correction cycles and their re-derivation cost; an explicit gate-level disposition would have surfaced the fix-or-accept decision when the finding was cheapest to act on.

observations.observation: The release evidence set was not batched: the first correction (21.7) was followed by a full artifact/live/security re-derivation (21.8-21.10), and only then did the next security review find the second correction set (21.11), requiring a second full re-derivation (21.12-21.14). No harness rule requires a consolidated adversarial pass before re-deriving, so the protocol ran twice at full cost.
evidence: docs/implementation/orchestrator-sessions (the 'Starting phase 21' session is the largest of the release)
observations.proposed_change: Add an orchestration rule (docs/agent-contracts.md or docs/plan/README.md release lifecycle) that a release candidate with an open corrective finding set does not begin the artifact/live/security re-derivation until a consolidated adversarial review of the fix batch reports no further open BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM, or the user explicitly accepts re-running.
observations.rationale: One consolidated pass would have saved an entire re-derivation cycle's cost and delay; the records show the second batch was discoverable by the same review class.

observations.observation: The task 15.4 worker was dispatched on a task whose acceptance criteria required a security review, but the worker session (depth-1 subagent) could not delegate to the security-reviewer; it correctly returned BLOCKED without fabricating a review, and the orchestrator then ran the review itself. This is an unhandled harness/contract interaction at least once.
evidence: docs/implementation/15.4/orchestration.json (implementation-worker attempt 1 BLOCKED; note: 'subagent(security-reviewer) and subagent(general) were both refused')
observations.proposed_change: State in docs/agent-contracts.md that a task whose acceptance criteria include a specialist review must be flagged in its task brief as orchestrator-run, and that a depth-1 implementation-worker must not attempt to delegate (return BLOCKED with the required delegation and let the orchestrator dispatch it).
observations.rationale: Prevents the same wasted worker attempt and the ambiguity about whether the review is the worker's or the orchestrator's responsibility.

observations.observation: Task 21.11 recorded two attempt-0 sessions that FAILED without producing a report (worker and reviewer), consistent with an infrastructure/provider abort rather than a task outcome; both were retried and completed. Task 21.6's orchestration record does not exist because the task remains open, so its executed worker/reviewer sessions are not represented in the aggregate measurements above.
observations.proposed_change: Add a short note to the orchestrator runbook in docs/agent-contracts.md: retry an attempt-0 invocation whose report is absent before treating it as a failed attempt, and ensure the final release task's orchestration record is written before the release-phase aggregate, even when the task's completion is gated on the release review.
observations.rationale: Makes the retry policy explicit and keeps the release aggregate complete for the next agent-process audit.

accepted_limitations: F5 - the renderer depends on a host-supplied SkiaSharp with no bundled fallback. Consequence: a host without a compatible SkiaSharp fails closed (current artwork preserved). Evidence: docs/limitations/accepted.md F5; ADR-015. Also an explicit v1.2 exclusion.

P1 - byte-reproducibility depends on the pinned toolchain (.NET SDK 10.0.x validated with 10.0.401). Consequence: a different SDK could change the bytes. Evidence: docs/limitations/accepted.md P1; this review's reproduction. NOTE: P1's wording still calls 1.1.0.0 the current identity and must be refreshed post-gate (RR-V12-2).

P2 - the shipped assembly has reduced debug metadata for reproducibility (no commit suffix / no SourceLink mapping). Consequence: source-level debugging of a released assembly is harder. Evidence: accepted.md P2; docs/release/build-and-release.md.
P3 - PackagePlugin=true stages but does not write the archive. Consequence: the documented ./build.sh package entry point must be used. Evidence: accepted.md P3.
P4 - SkiaSharp license notices ship although SkiaSharp is no longer redistributed. Consequence: extra license text in the package. Evidence: accepted.md P4; ADR-015.
P5 - pre-release orphaned state and uninstall drain behavior. Consequence: an operator must remove a retained state root or reconcile on reinstall. Evidence: accepted.md P5.
P6 - the v1.1.0 publication, manifest push and asset upload remain pending. Consequence: catalog installation of 1.1.0 is not live. Evidence: accepted.md P6 (a user-manual step).
V1 - no live Sonarr or Radarr release instance. Consequence: payload-shape variance beyond the committed fixtures is untested. Evidence: accepted.md V1.
V2 - the ADR-010 non-canonical cross-runtime comparison is unselected and unrun. Consequence: the tolerance half of the oracle is not executed. Evidence: accepted.md V2.
V3 - Jellyfin Enhanced coexistence is contract-level only. Consequence: live overlap behavior in an Enhanced install is unverified. Evidence: accepted.md V3.
V4 - live IProviderManager.SaveImage read-back is manual, not an automated live test. Evidence: accepted.md V4.
V5 - live Plugin.OnUninstalling drain has no automated live test. Evidence: accepted.md V5.
V6 - host-guarded facts are skipped without the pinned host. Evidence: accepted.md V6; the default suite's 66 skips.
D1 - webhook 401 bodies carry framework problem+json detail rather than ADR-012's 'no body' wording. Evidence: accepted.md D1.
D2 - ArtworkSubjectGate has no idle eviction. Evidence: accepted.md D2.
RR-1 - Phases 1-3 have no independent phase-review records. Evidence: accepted.md RR-1.
RR-15 - mock fixture API keys appear in tracked documentation. Evidence: accepted.md RR-15.
SEC-2 - state-root resolution falls back to a shared temp path when the host supplies no data folder (not reachable on the pinned host; carried as SEC-21.5-04). Evidence: accepted.md SEC-2.
SEC-3 - the state-envelope integrity hash does not cover envelope metadata (corruption detection, not tamper authentication). Evidence: accepted.md SEC-3.
SEC-4 - authentication error bodies carry framework problem+json detail. Evidence: accepted.md SEC-4.
SEC-5 - secrets persist only in Jellyfin's plugin configuration XML; ArrTags logging is bounded and redacted. Evidence: accepted.md SEC-5.
SEC-6 - the ArtworkSubjectGate process-lifetime bound. Evidence: accepted.md SEC-6.
SEC-7 - a declared non-JSON content type is rejected with a bounded 400. Evidence: accepted.md SEC-7.
SEC-8 - no per-client authentication throttling on the anonymous webhook route. Evidence: accepted.md SEC-8.
SEC-9 - configuration-rejection activity-log surfacing is bounded and secret-free. Evidence: accepted.md SEC-9.
SEC-10 - configured provider API keys and the webhook secret are not length-bounded. Evidence: accepted.md SEC-10.
SEC-11 - library-scope entries are not count/length-bounded or validated as library identifiers. Evidence: accepted.md SEC-11.
SEC-12 - configured base-URL user information is not rejected (it is excluded from the connection identity). Evidence: accepted.md SEC-12.
P12R-F1 - the absolute default output-fingerprint pin lives only in the forced-native golden path. Evidence: accepted.md P12R-F1.
V11-G1 - the badge value allowlist was not exercised live. Evidence: accepted.md V11-G1.

Evidence: accepted.md V12-F4-1..6; ADR-022/ADR-029.

F-21.13-2 (NEW; registration required, RR-V12-1) - an item whose active image content hash changes (a host refresh re-adopts the local sidecar) is moved to the fail-closed ownership state and v1.2 has no in-product recovery trigger; automatic publication for that item is suppressed until an out-of-band action. Consequence: operators must complete library/refresh setup before the first publication and use the scheduled trigger afterwards; a lost item needs an out-of-band recovery. Evidence: docs/implementation/21.13/live-verification.json F-21.13-2; docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md lines 342-352/457-475; docs/changelog/v1.2.0.md. To be registered in docs/limitations/accepted.md + 00-index.md in the release commit.

The tag may proceed on this SHIP decision.
summary: The ArrTags 1.2.0.0 release candidate is safe to ship with its accepted limitations. I independently reproduced the artifact from git archive HEAD of the reviewed commit (b58f246): byte-identical SHA-256/MD5/size/7-entry archive, 0 warnings/0 errors, and the packaged ArrTags.dll byte-identical to a clean build of the audited source. All four recorded suite tiers reproduce (default 0/1,966/66/2,032; host-guarded 0/1,986/46/2,032; forced-native 0/2,053/21/2,074; the no-archive tier is verified by the 21.12 reviewer). The live pinned-host matrix was independently re-run end to end against this exact artifact: install/load 1.2.0.0 with no [FTL]/[ERR], all three items published at Extra Large through the host image path with served bytes equal to the persisted ActiveImageIdentity, unchanged metadata did not republish while changed metadata did, a simultaneous provider outage left the host up with images byte-unchanged, a restart preserved state byte-for-byte, the uninstall drain restored the source posters and removed install/state, and every source media file was byte-unchanged throughout. The release security review (21.14) is APPROVED with 0 open BLOCKER/HIGH and SEC-21.5-01/-02/-03 resolved by reproduction against the shipped assembly; the only carried security item (SEC-21.5-04) is the already-accepted SEC-2. Phase gates 15-20 are met with tags and no open BLOCKER/HIGH, Gate 21's clauses are met except the tag that this gate authorizes, and check-docs/render-docs-state pass at HEAD. Two required post-gate documentation changes remain (register F-21.13-2; advance current_release and refresh P1), both documentation/state only and foldable into the release commit without touching the verified artifact. Decision: SHIP_WITH_ACCEPTED_LIMITATIONS; the annotated tag v1.2.0 may proceed.
limitations_accepted: F5 - the renderer depends on a host-supplied SkiaSharp with no bundled fallback. Consequence: a host without a compatible SkiaSharp fails closed (current artwork preserved). Evidence: docs/limitations/accepted.md F5; ADR-015. Also an explicit v1.2 exclusion.

P1 - byte-reproducibility depends on the pinned toolchain (.NET SDK 10.0.x validated with 10.0.401). Consequence: a different SDK could change the bytes. Evidence: docs/limitations/accepted.md P1; this review's reproduction. NOTE: P1's wording still calls 1.1.0.0 the current identity and must be refreshed post-gate (RR-V12-2).

P2 - the shipped assembly has reduced debug metadata for reproducibility (no commit suffix / no SourceLink mapping). Consequence: source-level debugging of a released assembly is harder. Evidence: accepted.md P2; docs/release/build-and-release.md.
P3 - PackagePlugin=true stages but does not write the archive. Consequence: the documented ./build.sh package entry point must be used. Evidence: accepted.md P3.
P4 - SkiaSharp license notices ship although SkiaSharp is no longer redistributed. Consequence: extra license text in the package. Evidence: accepted.md P4; ADR-015.
P5 - pre-release orphaned state and uninstall drain behavior. Consequence: an operator must remove a retained state root or reconcile on reinstall. Evidence: accepted.md P5.
P6 - the v1.1.0 publication, manifest push and asset upload remain pending. Consequence: catalog installation of 1.1.0 is not live. Evidence: accepted.md P6 (a user-manual step).
V1 - no live Sonarr or Radarr release instance. Consequence: payload-shape variance beyond the committed fixtures is untested. Evidence: accepted.md V1.
V2 - the ADR-010 non-canonical cross-runtime comparison is unselected and unrun. Consequence: the tolerance half of the oracle is not executed. Evidence: accepted.md V2.
V3 - Jellyfin Enhanced coexistence is contract-level only. Consequence: live overlap behavior in an Enhanced install is unverified. Evidence: accepted.md V3.
V4 - live IProviderManager.SaveImage read-back is manual, not an automated live test. Evidence: accepted.md V4.
V5 - live Plugin.OnUninstalling drain has no automated live test. Evidence: accepted.md V5.
V6 - host-guarded facts are skipped without the pinned host. Evidence: accepted.md V6; the default suite's 66 skips.
D1 - webhook 401 bodies carry framework problem+json detail rather than ADR-012's 'no body' wording. Evidence: accepted.md D1.
D2 - ArtworkSubjectGate has no idle eviction. Evidence: accepted.md D2.
RR-1 - Phases 1-3 have no independent phase-review records. Evidence: accepted.md RR-1.
RR-15 - mock fixture API keys appear in tracked documentation. Evidence: accepted.md RR-15.
SEC-2 - state-root resolution falls back to a shared temp path when the host supplies no data folder (not reachable on the pinned host; carried as SEC-21.5-04). Evidence: accepted.md SEC-2.
SEC-3 - the state-envelope integrity hash does not cover envelope metadata (corruption detection, not tamper authentication). Evidence: accepted.md SEC-3.
SEC-4 - authentication error bodies carry framework problem+json detail. Evidence: accepted.md SEC-4.
SEC-5 - secrets persist only in Jellyfin's plugin configuration XML; ArrTags logging is bounded and redacted. Evidence: accepted.md SEC-5.
SEC-6 - the ArtworkSubjectGate process-lifetime bound. Evidence: accepted.md SEC-6.
SEC-7 - a declared non-JSON content type is rejected with a bounded 400. Evidence: accepted.md SEC-7.
SEC-8 - no per-client authentication throttling on the anonymous webhook route. Evidence: accepted.md SEC-8.
SEC-9 - configuration-rejection activity-log surfacing is bounded and secret-free. Evidence: accepted.md SEC-9.
SEC-10 - configured provider API keys and the webhook secret are not length-bounded. Evidence: accepted.md SEC-10.
SEC-11 - library-scope entries are not count/length-bounded or validated as library identifiers. Evidence: accepted.md SEC-11.
SEC-12 - configured base-URL user information is not rejected (it is excluded from the connection identity). Evidence: accepted.md SEC-12.
P12R-F1 - the absolute default output-fingerprint pin lives only in the forced-native golden path. Evidence: accepted.md P12R-F1.
V11-G1 - the badge value allowlist was not exercised live. Evidence: accepted.md V11-G1.
V11-G2/G3/G4 - carried Phase 11-13/release LOW residuals. Evidence: accepted.md.
V12-G6-1 - a legacy in-range off-step byte limit loads unchanged and is re-quantized or rejected on the next save (the step check is page-side only). Evidence: accepted.md V12-G6-1; ADR-028.
V12-G8-1 - the restart-required modal reminder is a best-effort web-client shim verified structurally. Evidence: accepted.md V12-G8-1.
V12-G8-2 - the global OperationalLimits.RequestTimeoutSeconds is inert (per-connection values govern). Evidence: accepted.md V12-G8-2.
V12-F3-1 - the diagnostics panel is verified structurally, not executed. Evidence: accepted.md V12-F3-1.

V12-F4-1..6 - cursor resume is O(offset) per run / O(N^2/QueueCapacity) per full cycle; ties on (SortName, Name) have no host-guaranteed order; the cursor is a Cache record subject to render-cache age pruning; an unlocatable anchor resets to the start; the resume relies on the pinned host's internal candidate order; overlapping whole-scope runs are not cross-run locked. Evidence: accepted.md V12-F4-1..6; ADR-022/ADR-029.
V12-F6-1 - the configuration version can advance between metadata publication and the artwork stage of the same pass. Evidence: accepted.md V12-F6-1.
V12-F6-2 - the stale-basis re-enqueue's bounded drop is not logged or counted. Evidence: accepted.md V12-F6-2.

F-21.13-2 (NEW; registration required, RR-V12-1) - an item whose active image content hash changes (a host refresh re-adopts the local sidecar) is moved to the fail-closed ownership state and v1.2 has no in-product recovery trigger; automatic publication for that item is suppressed until an out-of-band action. Consequence: operators must complete library/refresh setup before the first publication and use the scheduled trigger afterwards; a lost item needs an out-of-band recovery. Evidence: docs/implementation/21.13/live-verification.json F-21.13-2; docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md lines 342-352/457-475; docs/changelog/v1.2.0.md. To be registered in docs/limitations/accepted.md + 00-index.md in the release commit.
